inlines.text: lie on the same line. Three points
have the same gradient, because then
are parallel lines passing through a common point

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}m_{AB}&=\frac{3-5}{1-(-2)}\\m_{AB}&=-\frac{2}{3}\\m_{BC}&=\frac{-1-3}{7-1}\\m_{BC}&=-\frac{4}{6}\\m_{BC}&=-\frac{2}{3}\end{align*}$$
The gradients are equal, so the points are collinear.

answer.short: Not collinear; the gradients are $-2$ and $-\frac{7}{3}$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}m_{PQ}&=\frac{1-7}{1-(-2)}\\m_{PQ}&=\frac{-6}{3}\\m_{PQ}&=-2\\m_{QR}&=\frac{-6-1}{4-1}\\m_{QR}&=-\frac{7}{3}\end{align*}$$
The gradients are different, so the points are not collinear.

$$\begin{align*}m_{PQ}&=\frac{-2-(-4)}{-2-(-5)}\\m_{PQ}&=\frac{2}{3}\\m_{QR}&=\frac{0-(-2)}{1-(-2)}\\m_{QR}&=\frac{2}{3}\end{align*}$$
The gradients are equal, so the points are collinear.
